I cannot recommend The Witcher 3 enough, it one of the best videogame experiences I have ever had, with a super immersive world and an insane amount of content.

One of the best things about the game, is there are no 'garbage' quests; In most RPGs they will have really shitty side quests all over the place, ones with either shitty story or no story, and often with crappy repetitive gameplay. In The Witcher 3, EVERY quest feels completely fleshed out and realized, each with an interesting little piece of story, interesting combat/solutions, and ultimate fully-realized experiences.

Going into the game, the Contract missions (where some bloke posts a notice paying for some monster to be killed), one would expect those missions to be the perfect place to dump garbage missions, but NOPE, even those missions feel fully realized with interesting little stories and fun unique combat engagements, I don't know how they managed to put so much detail into each quest (and there are a LOT of quests).

-tho to be fair, the Treasure Hunt quests are the one set of quests that feel a tad shallow like typical RPD quests, but those are a very small part of the game

The one asterisk I would put on this game is, it is a slow-paced RPG that spends a lot of time building up the narrative and immersion; if you are wanting a fast-paced shoot-em-up experience with only wall-to-wall action, this game might seem a bit tedious for your tastes.

In the PS2 title Shadow of the Colossus, the protagonist's horse Argo had some very unique AI that until then was not a common thing to see in ridable steeds.

  • Agro will stop if she comes to a drop that is too big to jump, will turn and steer around objects by herself whilst the player rides her and will slow down if she is traveling across, for example, a narrow path (such as the natural bridge that leads to Kuromori's lair).

  • If the player points his bow and arrow at Agro, Agro will rear up and neigh before galloping away and out of the line of fire.

Most of the games that I've played treat a mount as a simple extension of the playable character's movement. Usually only augmenting the movement speed to give the impression of being atop a creature with a longer stride.

But for Shadow of the Colossus (and the upcoming WiiU Legend of Zelda game in fact), the horse possessed just enough realistic behaviors that she went from a simple speed boost to a real character, one capable of self-preservation and insight into her place in the world.
